newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 17.54 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 17.54 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs rose 105 basis points to 17.54 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters using the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 60 billion bolivars of 180- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 16.48 percent coupon for a price of 99.51 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 16.48 percent.

The bank also sold 10 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 16.81 percent coupon at a price of 97.02 percent, and 10 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 17.15 percent coupon at an average price of 95.32 percent.
Yields for these notes rose 42 basis points to 212.44 percent for the 269-day bills, and 71 basis points to 22.93 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
